claim: For the countable metric star \(S=\bigvee_{i\in\mathbb N}[0,\infty)_i\) with all origins identified and the path metric, let \(\mathcal C(S)\) be the nonempty closed connected subsets with the extended Hausdorff topology. Its connected components coincide with its path-connected components and are exactly the finite-Hausdorff-distance classes; for origin-containing sets with endpoint profiles \(a,b\in[0,\infty]^{\mathbb N}\), these classes are characterized by \(\{i:a_i=\infty\}=\{i:b_i=\infty\}\) and \(\sup_{i:a_i<\infty}|a_i-b_i|<\infty\). There are exactly \(2^{\aleph_0}\) components.

correctness.rationale: The proof classifies every member of \(\mathcal C(S)\), derives the exact profile distance formula, proves finite-distance classes are clopen, constructs paths within each class, and gives matching continuum lower and upper bounds. The non-centre cases (bounded intervals and tails) are explicitly joined to canonical profiles by continuous paths.

evidence: Cauty (2011), pp. 91–92: for a connected noncompact metric space with convex metric and compact closed bounded subsets, components of the full hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets containing unbounded sets are homeomorphic to a nonseparable Hilbert space; Lemma 1 identifies components with finite-Hausdorff-distance classes under those hypotheses.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither theorem covers the exact claim. The countable star fails properness because its closed bounded ball around the origin contains an infinite uniformly separated family, and the present hyperspace is restricted to connected closed subsets, including unbounded ones. Curtis's compact-subset hyperspace omits these unbounded sets.

value.rationale: The countable star is the natural infinite-ray boundary of the established finite-ray model. The exact quotient by bounded endpoint-profile difference explains a phenomenon absent with finitely many rays: unbounded growth across infinitely many individually bounded arms creates continuum many components. This is a precise structural invariant useful for understanding noncompact hyperspaces; it is not merely a parameter substitution because the component invariant changes from a finite direction set to a profile quotient.
